quests.title: Hidden in the Shadows

dialogue.t: It's been a few days since we said bye to the others in Nasha Town.
Still no news about Rerir, though. Where could he have slunk off to?
If only he was gone for good... But with all the trouble he stirred up before, there's no way we've seen the last of him!
Hello! You must be the Traveler and Paimon?
Mr. Flins has been looking for you. Unfortunately, there's been a serious Wild Hunt attack over at the quarry. He thinks it's time to regroup and figure out a plan.
The Wild Hunt!? Uh-oh, we'd better get over there, right away!
C'mon, let's go, {NICKNAME}!
I can barely sense any kuuvahki at all. This whole area feels like a soulless husk.
Looks like his appetite truly is insatiable. As if the power of that Energy Cannon wasn't enough...
He's not seriously still getting stronger!? What's his endgame here?
Ah, everyone's here already. Hey, we made it... So, what's going on?
We've all been on high alert since we split up a few days back, expecting Rerir to strike again.
But it's like he just vanished into thin air. No one has seen him, nor found any trace of his presence.

...That is, until this morning, when a Ratnik found signs of Wild Hunt activity while out here on patrol. As you can see, the Crystonite itself is physically intact, but the kuuvahki it contained is all but completely diminished.
And we're sure that Rerir did this?
Who else? He's the only one who could pull off a stunt like this...
Kuuvahki loss has reached critical levels. Rächer of Solnari set to maximum threat level.
Warning: Unless de-escalation measures are taken soon, he will pose a threat beyond our ability to contain. The consequences could be catastrophic.
{NICKNAME}, do you remember when we encountered Rerir just after regaining his body?
There wasn't a shred of sanity left — nothing but madness and rage.

dialogue.sit: I remember it well.
He was already extremely dangerous, even then...

dialogue.t: Yeah. Didn't he shout out a bunch of names? Then he started raving about how nothing in this world mattered to him...
Paimon gets chills just thinking about it. But the thought that he's still out there, lurking somewhere in Nod-Krai, waiting for his chance to strike... *shudder* Even chillier.
Last time we fought, we were already at a disadvantage. If he has such overwhelming strength, why would he suddenly go into hiding?
Yeah... If I were him, and I wanted more kuuvahki, I'd just take it by force. No point staying in the shadows.
Unless... something went wrong? His whole resurrection thing didn't exactly go smoothly.
The other thing is... how does someone who's completely lost their mind still have the wherewithal to cover their tracks so perfectly?
Beats me...
According to certain medical studies, insanity does not always entail a complete loss of rationality. It may be that he is simply living in a world of his own.
That... actually sounds about right. He was ranting away to himself the whole time, like he had zero interest in talking to us.
There are many unanswered questions here. He could be right under our noses, and we'd still be in the dark.
Besides his name and title, we know little about him. Certainly nothing about his past or what he might be hoping to achieve.
Exactly — and we wouldn't even know where to begin looking! Even boss hadn't heard of the "Rächer of Solnari" before all this.
I'd be willing to bet that even if we gathered together every scrap of intel in Nod-Krai, we still wouldn't find more than, like, three useful facts about him.
So if we do nothing, he'll just keep getting stronger... but if we wanna investigate him, we have no idea where to look.
Last time, we had Marionette and her big robo-buddy to help us, and we still barely held our ground. If we had to face him alone...
Ugh, Paimon's head hurts just thinking about it. What are we supposed to do against a threat this big?
Well, I do have a little hunch about his next move. Given that he attacked the quarry, I'd say it's likely he'll target other places rich in kuuvahki.
Somewhere like the Eye of Kratti, or the Pillar of Embla. One thing's for sure — if we just sit back and let him keep absorbing kuuvahki, we really won't stand a chance against him.
A perfectly reasonable hypothesis. However, it is worth noting that these two locations are quite far apart. To investigate them both, we'll need to split up.
I agree, we should split up. Right now, Rerir's goal seems to be gathering kuuvahki, not fighting us directly. Once we're done, let's regroup on Hiisi Island.
...Wait, why Hiisi Island?
If I recall correctly, your largest goddess statue was carved from kuuvahki-rich ore, was it not?
Hmm, that's right... Yes, it could well be a potential target of his. I should head back and start evacuating the pilgrims.
Splitting up's always gonna be risky, but I guess we don't have much choice, right? We're in a race against time here.
And if we do run into Rerir... What then?
Heh, that's when you follow the third rule of treasure hunting: Run like the wind!
Uh... Didn't you say the third rule was "go with the flow"?
Uhh... I dunno, did I? Anyway, whatever! In this situation, "go with the flow" means "go find backup."
Agreed. If anyone finds so much as a trace of Rerir, do not pursue him. Get out of the area and alert the rest of us as soon as possible. We need to put safety first.
Alright, we'd better get moving. C'mon Ineffa, let's go.
Any leads?
Nope, diddly-squat. No clues to where he might be hiding. It's like he's a ghost...
It feels like we're sitting on a powder keg that could go off at any second... Ugh, I hate this feeling! I'd rather face him head-on than be left hanging like this!
So you guys didn't find anything either?
*sigh* Not loving the word "either"... How about you, Flins?
I questioned a few Ratniki and eventually narrowed my investigation down to one suspicious individual. But by the time I got to his place, he was already gone.
Almost as if he knew someone was onto him... Either that, or he's just extremely cautious and doesn't stay in one place for long.
He's been biding his time for a while now... The question is, where or what is his next target?
No idea. Since regaining his body, he seems to have lost all interest in the fragment in my possession. If he did still want it, he's had plenty of chances to take it.
All we can do now is hope that Aino and Ineffa turn up some leads... Darn it, Rerir! If you've got the guts, come face me one-on-one!
...W—Wait, he's actually here!? I didn't mean it, I swear!
No, it's coming from...
...Silvermoon Hall! The Lady Kuu{RUBY#[S]Moon Maiden}tar might be in danger!
Let's get over there, quick!
Th—That was too close...
We barely made it out of there alive! What's that guy's deal? How'd he get so crazy strong?

dialogue.sit: He's one of the Five Sinners...
...And that probably wasn't his full strength.

dialogue.t: He's a threat to this entire nation. I doubt his strength could even be measured by conventional standards.
I have a question.
When me and Ineffa showed up, we saw him chasing after this lady like he wanted her dead. What was that all about?
We weren't there for the whole thing either. They were already duking it out by the time we arrived.
Yeah, we didn't see how it all started. It all escalated so quickly, we had no choice but to step in.
Kuu{RUBY#[S]Moon Maiden}tar, can you shed any light on the situation?
Kuutar... Cross-checking database... I see. So you're the one that the Frostmoon Scions refer to as the "Moon Goddess"?
(Wait, she's the Moon Goddess!? Ohhh, no wonder she looks just like all those statues...)
There are many reasons why people might worship the moon... and just as many why they might despise it.
I've never met that person before, but there was no mistaking his deep-seated hostility towards me.
Why he holds me in such contempt, I cannot say. But since he hunts the power of the moon... it's no surprise that I am a target.
Kuu{RUBY#[S]Moon Maiden}tar...
There are many potential motives. For instance, you helped {NICKNAME} escape his grasp. This could be his way of taking revenge.
It is also possible that he covets the kuuvahki inside you, and seeks to take it for his own. The list goes on.
But right now, devising a counter-strategy should be our number one priority. The likelihood of this location being discovered is close to 100%.
(A counter-strategy? But we don't stand a chance against an enemy like this...)
(Surely, our only option is to run? He's not gonna chase us to the end of the world, right? So, as long as we can sneak out of Nod-Krai undetected...)
(...No, I can't say that! Come on, Jahoda, this is serious stuff... You can't suggest we all just chicken out!)
Running is our only option.
Huh!?
You seem surprised... But what other choice do we have? We are facing an enemy we cannot possibly defeat in battle.
W—Well, I mean, yeah... but still...
It's not too late. I can distract him, so you'll have plenty of time to make your escape.
Wait, what? You're gonna act as bait!?
Doesn't that make sense? I'm the one he's after. There's no need for you to risk your necks on my behalf.
A coyote doesn't stop for bypassers while it's howling at the moon.
What is it, Lauma?
The Frostmoon Scions have already grown accustomed to life without their Goddess. My presence here is no longer essential, and this is not my home, so you needn't ask me to stay.
We can't just roll over and let him get away with this! That's not our style!
Yeah! We can't just call it quits after everything we've been through together!
(Besides, she pretty much saved my life back there. If I just ditched her now, I'd never forgive myself!)

We can't overlook that you have saved our lives multiple times now. To talk of returning the favor would be a little crass for my liking, but... suffice to say that we are friends, and friends look out for one another.
Rerir's true objective remains unclear. Even if we were to sacrifice Miss Kuu{RUBY#[S]Moon Maiden}tar, there's no guarantee he would stop.

dialogue.sit: Running away won't solve anything.
We stand and fight, no matter what.

dialogue.t: But—
Kuu{RUBY#[S]Moon Maiden}tar... I know why you left the Frostmoon Scions so long ago. It was because people started treating prayer as a form of trade.
They would make self-centered wishes, force you to accept meaningless offerings in return, and then expect you to perform miracles for them as if that were their entitlement.
If it were me, I might have walked away too. But I believe that time can change everything... and that sometimes, it takes losing something precious to appreciate its true worth.
After much reflection, I've realized that this was never about whether the Frostmoon Scions "need" you.
Any relationship based on need is purely transactional. What I truly hope... is that you'll choose to stay, not out of obligation, but as part of our family.
You were born here, and now you've returned. Who knows, perhaps it was the moonlight that guided you home.
Thank you, Lauma, but my power is on the wane. I'm afraid I will be of little use to you now.

dialogue.sit: We'll find a way.
It's our turn to help you now.

dialogue.t: ...Very well then. I'll do as you say.
Both times you saved us, we were transported across great distances in an instant. Is that one of your powers as the Moon Goddess?
It is, but I find it very draining. I barely managed to pull it off just now... and it will be some time before I'm strong enough to do so again.
Rejected by the world, my power is dwindling — like a lake cut off from its source, slowly shrinking away. Now... it has almost run dry.
What do you mean, "rejected by the world"?
The three moons belonged to the ancient, bygone era in which they came into being. From the moment I was born, the world itself has been steadily sapping away at my strength.

dialogue.sit: That's why we need the Moon Marrow — to borrow the Eternal Moon's power...

dialogue.t: The three moons are not one and the same. As the Goddess of the Frost Moon, I cannot wield the powers of the other two.
Yet moonlight has a way of blending together. Each can reflect the others' glow. So when our fingers touched, I was able to restore my strength by drawing kuuvahki from the Eternal Moon's marrow.
But this method of recovery is painfully slow. If only we could find th—
Raargh!
It's the Wild Hunt!
Ugh, even faster than we expected. We'll have to finish this conversation later.
Hmm... See how those Wild Hunt creatures are running away from us? They're likely just a scouting party... Which means, Rerir won't be far behind.
Then what are we waiting for? Let's get the heck outta here!
What's the matter, bit off more than you could chew?
Wh—Who the...
Uhh... Who are you?
Uncle Varka! You're back from Amsvartnir?
Whoa, you're Varka? Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius!?
We can save the intros for later. Right now, let's get you all out of this hellhole. Follow me — I know somewhere you'll be safe.
Oh, is that where I think it is?
That's the one. C'mon, move — there's no time to waste!
Wow, where are we? This is so well-hidden...
Heh, well that goes without saying. This is the Knights of Favonius's meeting place in Nod-Krai, and a contact hub for the Northern Intelligence Network.

dialogue.sit: The Northern Intelligence Network...

dialogue.t: ...Aka, the black market of intel. No matter what faction you're with, it's THE place to buy and sell information. Their headquarters are in Nod-Krai, but they've got contacts in every nation.
As an expeditionary force on foreign soil, working with them has offered us the most effective way of getting our hands on reliable local intel. This is where we meet — so naturally, it's secure.
Anyway, where were we? Folks from Nod-Krai should be pretty familiar with me by now, but I believe this is the first time we've met.
Allow me to introduce myself. I am Varka, Knight of Boreas, and Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius.
Hehe, we've heard all about you. This meeting's been a long time coming!
You look way younger than Paimon expected! But you definitely have that Grand Master vibe, hehe.
Haha, well, I'm no spring chicken. Just not showing my age yet.
Definitely feeling some of that back pain today, though... Rushed back from Amsvartnir without a wink of sleep, only to get right into another fight with that freshly revived maniac...
Another? You mean, you've fought him before?
Yep. He wasn't nearly as strong back then, but he was still a formidable foe. I brought some of the Knights along to give him a little "surprise," but he saw us coming from a mile off.
My squad took heavy injuries, and I barely made it out alive myself. We knew it might have been our last chance, so we staked everything on it... But still, it wasn't enough to stop him.
I tried tracking him down afterwards, but he didn't leave a trace. Even in his unhinged mental state, he's as cautious as any trained operative...
So I decided to come find you, and as luck would have it, turned up to find you being ambushed by the Wild Hunt. The rest, you already know.
Hmm... Is that why he's been frantically absorbing kuuvahki these past few days? Because he sees you as a threat?
Maybe I'm part of the equation, but even if I weren't, I'm sure he'd still be gathering power. He's clearly working up towards something.
Note to self: Uncle Varka's strength rating officially upgraded.
Guess it's my turn to ask questions now... So, what exactly's been happening in Nod-Krai? Why has the Wild Hunt returned in humanoid form, and why is it after you?
That's a long story, but I'll try to make it quick...

dialogue.sit: Aino brings Varka up to speed about what happened before...

dialogue.t: Wow, I had no idea so much had happened. Sounds like you guys have really been through it.
So, the Kuu{RUBY#[S]Moon Maiden}tar is actually a Fatui Harbinger... and all this Wild Hunt activity in Nod-Krai is the work of the "Rächer of Solnari," one of the Five Sinners...
That's a lot to take in. Need some time to wrap my head around it all...
I'm truly sorry, Mr. Varka.

You stood with us against the Wild Hunt, and did everything you could to stop it from escalating into a full-blown catastrophe. And then, the one time you're away, it all comes to a head and all your hard work gets undone...
You've got nothing to apologize for, Miss Moonchanter.
You can plan a hundred steps ahead and still slip up — that's just life. No one knows what tomorrow holds. You can't predict which way the wind will blow next.

And to be perfectly honest, I can't say I'm surprised. For all the times we've defeated the Wild Hunt in the past, we've never been able to completely wipe it out. Turns out we were just delaying the inevitable.
But now that a new variable has come into play, fate may well take a different course.
A new variable? You mean... us?

Heh, who else? And in a strange way, I think his resurgence might not be an entirely bad thing. The Wild Hunt is like an unrelenting force of nature, but Rerir is an individual with an agenda. He's gotta have a weak spot somewhere.
That said, while Aino was explaining everything just now, some of the points that Mr. Flins added caught my attention.
You mean about our mystery ally?
That's right. From what you've said, not only did they lead you straight to some key files, they also shielded Hiisi Island from a lethal kuuvahki blast.
I don't know who or what could pull something like that off... Heck, even Miss Columbina doesn't have a clue.
I hadn't heard the story about those files... Would you mind repeating their titles for me?
"Wild Hunt Phenomena Log," "A Nod-Kraian Ratnik's Field Journal," and "Kuuvahki Survey Log"...
Oh... No, still doesn't ring a bell...
Hmm, another dead end... Guess all we can do now is hope that our mystery ally keeps showing up when we most need them.
Still, it's safest to assume they won't be intervening again. From here on out, we'll have to resolve this crisis by ourselves.
Your intel also explains something else I've been wondering about. The reason I led my team to Amsvartnir was because we'd had reports about a possible source of the Wild Hunt showing up there.
But once we looked into it, it turned out to be a red herring. I don't know who was behind it, but clearly, it served its purpose.

I doubt it's by chance that he happened to make his comeback while my attention was diverted. And from everything you've told me, it sounds like his scheming began well before his return... so maybe luring me away was all a part of his plan.
(But is it even possible that he orchestrated all of this by himself?)
(The Moon Maiden and the Rächer of Solnari, in Nod-Krai of all places... The way everything is unfolding, it can't be a coincidence.)
So... What do we do now? Got any ideas?
Right now, we've got at least three things to consider. Let's go through them one by one.
First, we need to figure out how to take down Rerir. If we can't beat him in a straight-up fight, the rest won't even matter.

To my knowledge, the bulk of Nod-Krai's fighting force is already gathered here. But even with everyone united, we're still no match for Rerir in his current state — let alone with his power still growing.
...What if there was a way to tap into a new power of our own?
How so?
Have you thought of something, Columbina?
Three moons once watched over this world: the Eternal Moon was the largest, the Frost Moon was the brightest, and the Iridescent Moon was the most mysterious.
They say that back then, the three Moon Goddesses wielded immense power. Enough to shape the workings of the world itself.
I now bear the Frost Moon's power, and the Eternal Moon's marrow resides within {NICKNAME}.
Hold on, are you suggesting...
The Iridescent Moon, the last piece in the puzzle...
That's right. If we can find the Iridescent Moon's marrow, I will be able to regain my strength much more quickly.
The three moons are said to stir the tides and illuminate all things. Perhaps they hold further secrets beyond our understanding.
According to my analysis, this solution is feasible. However, it is subject to one major condition — how do we locate the Iridescent Moon's marrow?
I know a way, but... We will need to visit the Fatui's Experimental Design Bureau.
The Experimental Design Bureau? Are you saying... we need to involve Marionette?
Yes. I must speak with Sandrone.
It's a long way from here to the Experimental Design Bureau... There's a high chance you'll be spotted. You shouldn't go alone.

dialogue.sit: I will go with her.

dialogue.t: Then that's settled. Next up, our second priority — somehow, we need to figure out Rerir's end goal.

As you saw for yourselves, when he was still in his Wild Hunt form, everything he did was for the sake of recovering his body and resurrecting himself. His first act since then, after laying low for a while, was to try and assassinate this young lady.
People's obsessions often reveal their greatest vulnerabilities. There must be a reason why he despises the moon so deeply... Perhaps it'd shed some light on his title, the "Rächer of Solnari."
The Wild Hunt has plagued Nod-Krai for centuries now. If we want to stop it for good, we have to get to the root cause of what's driving it.
It's true... We still know very little about him.
If Kuu{RUBY#[S]Moon Maiden}tar hadn't given us that lead, we wouldn't even know his name.
But where would we even start? I doubt even the intel queen of Nod-Krai has a clue, and she has info coming out of her ears...
Oh? That's a rather hasty conclusion for someone who's so painstakingly meticulous when it comes to dealing with machines.
Ah, she heard me...
Boss! What are you doing here?

I'm now asking myself the same question... I received a letter from a "humble knight of Favonius," requesting a meeting to discuss a major business deal. But it looks like this humble knight had something else in mind.
Hahaha, details, details... Miss Nefer, the important thing is that you've arrived at the perfect time.

Since his failed ambush, I've been racking my brains trying to come up with a plan to fight Rerir. Given the severity of the situation, I think it's fair to say that our only chance lies in uniting as one — and I'm talking ALL the factions in Nod-Krai.
We can't do this without the Curatorium, but I knew it'd be a tough job to win you over. So I took the liberty of reaching out for a little chat.
Wait a sec... How did you even hear about this place, Nefer?
Didn't you say this is meant to be the Knights of Favonius's meeting spot, and a contact hub for the Northern Intelligence Network? And... isn't it supposed to be super hidden?
You really think he could've gotten settled in Nod-Krai without my help? Besides, I'm the one running this gig — of course I know where the meeting place is.

dialogue.sit: You mean...
You're...!

dialogue.t: Allow me to introduce the current head of the Northern Intelligence Network. If it's intel you're after, she's your woman. Pretty much seen and heard it all.
Please, spare me the flattery. Let's cut to the chase — seems like you've run into some trouble, huh?

dialogue.sit: You bring Nefer up to speed on what's been happening...

dialogue.t: Well, this certainly qualifies as an unforeseen crisis. On behalf of the Curatorium of Secrets... I wish you all the best of luck.
So you're just going to sit this one out?
Why should I get involved? What could possibly be in it for me?
What if we told you we can't do this without you?
Oh? Then I'd say, you'd better make it worth my while. I don't work for free.
I can't put a price on something like this — it's just not in my nature. But then again, you and I have always been polar opposites in this regard — so I can't exactly say I didn't see this coming.
If you insist on compensation, I will pay you. Consider this a formal commission. Sound fair?
You just don't give up, do you? Heh, too bad — I know you well enough to know you can't afford my prices.
The riskier the job, the more it'll cost, and a Moonchanter's stipend isn't exactly generous... Unless you're planning to start passing the donation box around among the faithful?
Uhh, boss, just a thought... If they come up short, maybe you can take the difference out of my next few paychecks?
Things got really dangerous during the fight with Rerir. If this girl hadn't saved me, I'd be ley line fodder by now... I'd be gone for good, boss.
If there's any way we can make this work, I'd really like to help her... Please, I'm begging you!
This is why I'm always telling you — never accept favors. They're the hardest debts to repay.
You have to be careful who you get involved with, or you invite all kinds of misfortune... *sigh* Very well, Jahoda, I will help — but just this once. Don't count on this happening again.
Flins, that fragment that Rerir was after... Do you still have it on you?
Of course.
Let me borrow it. I need it to follow up on some leads.
Wait... You actually have some leads!?
Shh... This is top-secret information.
I get it... We all have things we'd rather keep to ourselves. Plus, I know we can count on you, so we'll leave the intel-gathering in your hands.
And that brings me to the third and final item... We need to find a way to distract him. We need time to make our move, so someone will have to stall him.
I'm in for this part, no matter what. Anyone coming with?
Count me in too.
Come off it, you two... Quit playing heroes.
I'm waaay ahead of you here... Ineffa did a scan of the Moon Goddess's kuuvahki signature, and we're gonna use it to make some decoys over at the Krumkake Craftshop. Anyone who's "in," follow me.
Once they're ready, we'll deploy the decoys across Nod-Krai. So as long as the rest of you keep moving, he won't catch onto your scent and won't be able to track you down.
I like it! Genius idea.
No biggie!
Alright then, we'll split into three teams.
Once your team has finished their mission, return here and wait for the others. Dismissed!

quests.description: The “Rächer of Solnari” has been revived with the aid of a kuuvahki beam. Now a new crisis looms over Nod-Krai…

quests.title: Special Operation

dialogue.t: A mirror stands in the corner.
(Perhaps it's a window into Rerir's past.)

dialogue.sit: (test)台词文本

dialogue.t: Lady Damselette... Wait, and you two? What are you doing at the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau?
We've been doing our best to mind our own business lately, but if you're just gonna waltz up here like this, you're seriously pressing your luck. Don't blame us for doing what we have to.
Hmph! You really think that's gonna scare us off?
We're not looking for any trouble. I just want to see Sandrone...
...Do I need to remind you that you're still a wanted fugitive for deserting us?
Out of consideration for our former ties and the crisis we're all up against, we'll let you leave in one piece. But don't even think about trying to get insi—
Let them in.
But...
Are you going to make me repeat that?
N—No, my Lady...
Sandrone seems to be in a good mood. Must be maintenance day.
So, tell me. To what do I owe the honor this time?
...Actually, before you answer that... Just so we're clear — we're not colleagues anymore, Columbina. I don't owe you anything.
I promise it's nothing big.
It seems like you've gotten the wrong idea here. The only reason I let you in was because I was bored. It seemed like a way to kill some time and satisfy my own curiosity.
Whatever miscalculations I may or may not have made in the past, I haven't lost the plot enough to even consider sticking my neck out for your sakes.
I'd like to speak with Arlecchino.
...What?
Huh? You mean, The Knave!?
I'd like to speak with Arlecchino. Is she in Nod-Krai?

No, she's not. Once the work on this facility was completed, she went back with "The Rooster" and "Regrator." The only ones in Nod-Krai now are me, and... Ahem, what is it you need to speak to her about, anyway?
Rerir is hunting me. If I'm going to face him, I must first retrieve the lost moon.

dialogue.sit: (Marionette seems lost in thought, but she doesn't look surprised. She must know more than she was letting on.)
(I don't understand what Arlecchino has to do with the Iridescent Moon's marrow... But at this point, I have no choice but to go along with Columbina's plan.)

dialogue.t: Is that a no, then?

dialogue.sit: We're only doing this to stop Rerir.
...He is our common enemy.

dialogue.t: Hmph, as if I need reminding. I was THIS close to settling things with him before SOMEONE decided to whisk me away to their weird little garden.
Have you held any tea parties lately?
Tea parties? Uh, yeah, obviously. You don't seriously think we'd pack it all in just because you aren't here?
If anything, they've been more eventful than ever. Just me, Arlecchino, and a bunch of insolent, insensitive "guests" who won't stop asking where you've gone. Oh, they've been a real joy.
I bet you served them the worst tea you have. Just like you used to do to me when I upset you.
Hmph... Who cares about how good the tea is when there's no one around to drink it? I keep losing people...

First Rosalyne, now you... I'm running out of people who can make me laugh. Honestly, what could be more ridiculous than a multi-centenarian goddess who's only ever had the plain herbal tea she received as offerings? Heh...
You'd always brew a different type of tea for me each time. Was it really just to see how I'd react?
I, uh— Well, duh! Why else? Watching you squirm was practically my only form of entertainment.

dialogue.sit: (Or was she genuinely trying to introduce Columbina to new flavors? Maybe all that coldness is just an act... and they actually get along?)

dialogue.t: Oh, yeah... and Capitano sometimes used to bring Tartaglia around too, but I guess we won't be seeing him again.
Hmph... Well, I guess we are overdue for a get-together. Pulonia!
Have Fevroniya pass a message to Arlecchino for me. "It's time for tea" will suffice.
Pass along a message for me too, if you would: "My body cannot contain the marrow of two moons, so I'll be leaving one of them in her care."
Excuse me? Who said you were on the guest list? If my tea meant that much to you, maybe quitting the Fatui wasn't your brightest move.
Back when you were under the Tsaritsa's protection, no one would have dared come at you so openly.
But that protection didn't come for free — in fact, I paid dearly for it. At the end of the day, it was just another transaction.
I just got tired, that's all... I never wanted any part in their grand ambitions, and I've had enough of being treated like a bottomless supply of power.
It brings back memories from the old days, when I was still worshiped as the Moon Goddess. Centuries on, it may be a different group of people, but I see the same greed in their eyes.
Hmph... I figured you'd leave eventually. You didn't have as much of a reason to stay as I do.
The Tsaritsa gave you shelter and protection, but that was it — nothing more, nothing less. Meanwhile, the Fatui demanded everything from you in return, until it was more than you could bear.
I get why you left. And frankly, I have no interest in dragging you back just because the higher-ups told me to.
But if you keep hanging around with this riffraff, the next time we cross paths, we might be enemies for real.

dialogue.sit: (She says that, but she's the one who just caved in and agreed to help Columbina...)

dialogue.t: Heh... Well, uh... Guess that's our cue to leave?

dialogue.sit: Let's go.
We'd better not keep Varka and the others waiting.

dialogue.t: Umm... That might be your plan, but it sounds like someone else wants you to stay a little longer.
Huh? What do you mean?
See for yourselves.
Raargh!
My Lady, it's the Wild Hunt! A horde of monsters is headed straight for the facility!
Ugh. Another uninvited guest trying to crash my tea party. Clear the area — I'll handle this.
Wait, what? You want us to leave you here by yourself?
Heh, you'll be lucky to make it out of this alive. You really think you can afford to worry about me?
Go on, get out of here! You may have stopped Pulonia from crushing him last time, but I've made sure that won't happen again. The entire Experimental Design Bureau is rigged for war!
Stay and watch if you want — but it'll be at your own risk. You're not flagged as friendlies in the weapon system.

dialogue.sit: Just... be careful, okay?

dialogue.t: Don't tell me what to do! Look, if you're leaving, make it quick, or you'll just get in my way. There's a secret passage on the second floor — it'll take you right to the plains out back.
Stare all you want, Columbina. You're not getting another invitation to my tea party.
I know... But thank you anyway, Sandrone.
Ugh... This is exactly why you shouldn't hang around with those people. All their melodrama and sentimental nonsense is rubbing off on you.
Come on then, Mr. Rächer. Let's pick up where we left off.
It's your Wild Hunt monstrosities versus my beautiful creations... Let's see who comes out on top!
Hmph...
Pulonia, get him!
I've upgraded Pulonia again since our last encounter... and uploaded every last scrap of your data. So let's finish this, once and for—
She's not here...
Where did she go?
Hey, over here, you big—
Cursed... moon...
Go... Keep searching. She cannot have gotten far.
So this is your method for investigating Rerir's past? It almost looks like some kind of... ceremony.
Good deduction. But it's quite a different affair from what you're used to with the Frostmoon Scions.
(Whoa... First time I've ever been in here. Boss always said it was off-limits, so I pictured some kind of creepy dungeon... But it's actually kinda nice!)
(Oh! I guess this must be Sumeru decor? That's where boss is from... and that nice shopkeeper who sold me my treasure compass.)
I'm not sure exactly what you've got planned, but it looks like you're all set. When do we begin?
Whenever we wish... But for some reason, I've got a feeling this isn't going to end well.
I've never faced Rerir myself. But from what you've told me, his power is beyond anything I could imagine.
I, on the other hand, am just an ordinary businesswoman. Our paths should never have crossed, yet here I am, forced to make an enemy of him.
If you ask me, you're about as far from "ordinary" as it gets. So what are you saying? You're getting cold feet?
Once I take a job, there's no backing out. Still... I have to ask myself if the power I'm relying on will even work on an opponent of this caliber.
...And also, how to make sure I come out of this alive if things spiral out of control.
Death is the one thing we can take for granted. It is the great equalizer, however fortunate or unfortunate we may otherwise be. So it's important to consider how to spend what lifespan we have left.
Haha... C'mon boss, lighten up. Quit talking about death, it's bad luck!
...For once, I agree with you. When you're up against a foe like Rerir, there's no such thing as being too prepared.
Is there anything I can do to help?
That won't be necessary. I've already made up my mind... Time to cash in a precious favor I've been saving for a rainy day. Jahoda, I need you to find someone for me — the sooner, the better.
Eh? Find who?
That shady merchant who sold you an overpriced treasure compass the other day.

Come on, boss, you're pulling my leg again! In what way is she shady? She showed up when I was completely lost and sold me a neat little gadget that was exactly what I needed! Trust me, she's a good person!
Anyway, I know who you're talking about. Don't go anywhere, I'll be right back!

dialogue.sit: A few moments later...

dialogue.t: *panting* ...Quit dragging me, I genuinely can't run any further!
Hey, aren't you...
What is it? What's the big rush? You dragged me out of a dream where I was literally swimming in Mora... I—I'm charging double my usual attendance fee!
(See? Look how easygoing she is! After that rude awakening, she could've completely snapped at us, but instead she kept it together and just asked for an extra fee.)
Dori Sangemah Bay? I never would've pictured you two doing business together.
If you wanna make it big in Nod-Krai, it's all about connections. Lady Nefer just so happens to have a lot of intel that interests me — and she also did me a big favor in the past.
It was back when I first arrived in Nod-Krai. My trusty assistant, the Jinni in my lamp, had an adverse reaction to the kuuvahki and fainted.
And wouldn't you know it, that's when I suddenly find myself in a life-or-death situation. Good thing my compatriot was there to swoop in and save the day.

I've been giving her a thirty percent discount off all of my goods ever since. Now, so that no one here feels left out, I'm willing to extend a twenty percent discount to fellow friends of Boss Nefer.
Plus, any other friends you send my way will enjoy ten percent off. What can I say? The great Lord Sangemah Bay is nothing if not generous...
So, let me guess... You've run into some trouble? Hehe, I've got everything you could possibly need — and the more you buy, the more you'll save.
You guessed correctly. What have you got in the way of survival gear?
Heh, the one type of gear I've never been short on! What are you looking for? A jetpack fresh from the Akademiya's labs? An ancient suit of armor, dredged up from the bottom of the sea?
At the very least, I need to know what kind of opponent you're dealing with here. If even you're worried about staying alive, it must be pretty serious...
What if I told you it's someone with the power to bring a nation to its knees?
Is that so? Hmm... Then we really are talking top-shelf treasures. I don't have anything like that in stock right now... I'll have to ask my supplier.
Your supplier?
A powerful woman, make no mistake... I can't reveal her identity, but luckily for you, I hear she's planning to visit Nod-Krai in the near future.
If you're willing to wait, I can ask her once she's here. Can't say exactly how long that'll be, though...
Then let me put it another way... What would you do if you encountered an enemy like that? Roll over and serve yourself up on a silver platter?
Course not! I have a handy little trinket from one of my generous suppliers, which... Hold on, what exactly are you getting at? No, no, this is for my personal use only!
Let's just say I'm borrowing it, alright? Just for insurance purposes — you'll get it back later.
Favors are the worst kind of debt to owe, and now you've got a chance to repay one. A win-win situation, don't you think?
...Hmph, fine. You can borrow it for five days... No, make that three! And for every extra hour after that, I'm charging you a million Mora. Deal?
Deal.
*sigh* What a way to start the day... Now, was there anything else you wanted, or can I go back to bed now?
That will be all. Take care, now — don't trip up on your way back, friend.
See you later! You're my favorite shopkeeper!
Excellent, everything is well and truly ready. The ceremony can now begin.
After initiating the ceremony, your minds will follow me wherever I go. You will see many strange things in your mind's eye.
So remember: Don't be frightened, and don't make a sound...

dialogue.sit: After laying down the ground rules for everyone who will be joining the trip as a follower, Nefer begins the ceremony.

dialogue.t: Now then... Let us peer into the Rächer of Solnari's past.
(...I made it.)
(I don't recognize this style of architecture... Must be Khaenri'ahn.)
(Simple furnishings, table and chairs... It's a more ordinary house than I might have expected.)
(...Looks like the fearsome "Rächer of Solnari" came from surprisingly humble beginnings.)
(Unless this passed for luxury in Khaenri'ah...? Hmm, unlikely. It was said to be a very prosperous nation in its heyday.)
(...Anyway. I'll keep exploring.)
A handwritten note.
Hi, Rerir. Since you're working extra hours tonight, I thought I'd keep myself busy by checking out that new kebab shop. I've heard good things about their menu.
I'll test it out, and if it's as good as everyone's saying, let's go back together some time.
(P.S.: New stash from the Universitas Magistrorum. I brought some goodies home — a few teacups and a pen rack. Hope you like them!)
(They didn't sign their name... But they must have been close. Sounds like they were living together.)
A few storage boxes sit next to the cabinet. Everything in sight is neatly organized.
Whoever lives here seems to be enjoying a pretty comfortable life.
Rerir! Over here!
Dain! Oh, and... Vedrfolnir? What a surprise to see you here, Sir.
Hello there, Rerir. You need not address me so formally outside of court.
He doesn't get much free time, so I invited him over for a drink. Even the court prophet deserves a break every now and then, right?
Haha, well, I'm flattered.
So... What are we discussing today?
Hey, don't look at me. As far as I see it, we don't need an excuse to have a few drinks.
Come on, don't give us that! Didn't you say you were about to pop the big question? How's that coming along?
Heh, who'd have thought the great Twilight Sword was an even greater gossip?
I just didn't expect you to be the first one to settle down and get married, that's all.
Yeah... If you'd told me that a few years ago, I wouldn't have believed you either. Haha...
So, are you planning to come clean about your job, then? I'm guessing you still haven't told her.
Sure, I'll have to tell her at some point... but I'll need to pick the right time and place. To be honest, I have no idea how she'll take it.
Come on, stop being such a pessimist. For all you know, she could be thrilled! I bet she'll be much more impressed by your actual job than the one she thinks you're doing now.
A member of the "King's Guard"... Heh, quite the cover story. Does the king himself even know?
Of course he does. Anyway, enough about me. How've you been?
Me? Same old, same old, nothing much to— Huh?
What's up, Ved?
...It's nothing.
(Vedrfolnir, Dainsleif's elder brother... Renowned throughout the Court of Khaenri'ah as "The Visionary," and said to possess a wisdom far beyond the reach of any ordinary man.)
(And yet, despite the gulf between us, he seems to have something to say about me...)
(Does he even know me? Does he see me as a friend of his brother... or just another of the Vinster King's blades?)
(Why did he react so strongly? Was it really to do with what we were talking about?)
(Brown, curly hair, and brooding blue eyes. So this is what Rerir looked like back in the day.)
(Perfectly normal, no different from anyone else.)
(As frightening as this monster is in the present... There's something even more unsettling about seeing the human he used to be.)
Tholindis? You're back early.
Our equipment's being serviced today, so I got off earlier than usual. How's your day been?
Aw, why the long face? Is something the matter? Has your boss been giving you a hard time again?
Went for a drink with Dain and the others after work.
Isn't that a good thing?
Vedrfolnir showed up today too. You know, Dainsleif's older brother.
Ah, Mr. Vedrfolnir. Yes, I've heard of him. They say that everything he says ends up coming true.
...He overheard Dainsleif mention that I'd recently proposed, and seemed to have an issue with it. But when I asked what it was, he kept it to himself.
So... you're worried? You can be such a child sometimes, Rerir.
We're nobodies. Why would The Visionary be concerned about us?
I'm sure someone in his position has much bigger fish to fry.
Ha... Maybe you're right.
You worry too much, Rerir. We've been together for ages now, and everything's been going so well, has it not? You've even proposed to me!
Haha, so you do remember. Tell me, then... what's your answer?
Like I said, I need some time to decide. You can't just rush into things like this. We may be nobodies in the grand scheme of things, but if we want things to work out, we've still got to plan ahead.
Alright, take your time. Just don't keep me waiting forever.
("Nobodies"... Hmph, sounds about right. In the eyes of people like Vedrfolnir and Dainsleif, what do we matter?)

(Can someone whose gaze is so fixed on the far-flung future even see the present clearly? Besides... The dynasty's fate rests with the king and his inner circle. Whatever I do, it won't make much difference.)

(Meanwhile, every idea they come up with and every decision they make, it affects everything... These days, the king is lost in his research, and the purge of the Crimson Moon bloodline grows ever more intense.)
(The opposition tried to speak out, but nothing came of it. And I'm under no illusions as to why — because we eliminated them and got rid of their bodies.)
(A man can have a thousand reasons to carry a sword, but there are few good excuses to use it. Yet the king has never even considered a gentler approach, and he never will.)
(...What becomes of someone who kills on another's behalf? Can he ever find true peace?)
Tholindis... I...
*sigh* It's nothing. You are right... Fate has never smiled upon nobodies like us. But by the same token, it's unlikely to bear a grudge against us, either.
There's no reason we can't keep living happily together, cherishing the simple joys of each day as they come...
See? You just need to stay positive, Rerir.
I can feel your warmth, your breath... You're right there, right by my side.
Just seeing you makes me happy in a way I can't explain, and that's something that no one could ever take away from me. So smile, my love... Let go of that frown.
You're right, Tholindis. I've just been overthinking things.
That's better. Getting caught up about things like this will only ruin our evening. Speaking of which... All set for the ball tonight? I need to go get ready.
You go ahead. I just have a few things to take care of, then I'll come join you.
Even busier than the big shots, huh? Fine, I'll go get started... but don't be late. If you keep me waiting too long, I won't be a happy bunny.
Relax, I'll be there...
Seriously, though, you drive a hard bargain... You're really gonna leave my proposal hanging, and still expect me to take you to the ball?
Well that goes without saying. I already told everyone I'd be coming with a dance partner.
Besides, they're two completely different things... Let's take it one thing at a time, alright?
Hmph...
Alright, white outfit it is.
(It seems like Rerir was deliberately hiding his ties to the intelligence services... by giving the impression that he was just an ordinary member of the Vinster King's guard.)
(He clearly doesn't want his would-be fiancee to know about his other life. Then again, that's hardly surprising — people in the intelligence trade rarely do.)
(Heh, who'd have thought we were in the same line of work...)
(Let's dig a little deeper.)
Our last operation was a resounding success — and all thanks to you, Rächer of Solnari. In total, we apprehended 32 dregs of the Crimson Moon, and 67 accomplices.
After all these years since the dynasty's fall, so many of them still linger on.

Indeed, it cannot be denied. Yet it was destiny that the Crimson Moon should be overcome by the Eclipse, and that His Majesty, the all-seeing Vinster King, now guides our nation on the path to prosperity.
Khaenri'ah has no further need for a dead moon. But alas, there will always be those who refuse to see the truth, choosing instead to romanticize the past.
That's not entirely true. Much about the Crimson Moon era was worthy of remembrance, and that's exactly why they keep trying to see it restored.
Many of its secrets remain unsolved to this day. As it happens, that's precisely the field of study my partner is devoted to.
You still haven't told her what you really do for a living?
Where would I even start?
How do you tell someone that you're one of the king's hand-picked executioners? That your hands are steeped in blood?
You didn't choose this life, any more than I did. Orphans like us don't get a say.
But I'll sure as heck be the one to pay for it.
Speaking of which... We need to be more rigorous in the way we identify direct descendants of the Crimson Moon.
Someone, it seems, has strong opinions about my future plans — most likely my marriage, in particular. I have a feeling that we may soon become targets of the Crimson Moon's retribution.

Your concerns are not unfounded. They've taken out many of our colleagues these past few years, and for that very reason. These are no helpless lambs we're leading to the slaughter — they're wolves in sheep's clothing.
Take care, Rächer of Solnari. I look forward to toasting you at your wedding.
Thanks, Thorkell. You look after yourself too.
Tholindis, I never wanted to keep this from you. You're the last person I would ever want to lie to.
But that's exactly why I can't tell you everything. There are things you shouldn't know... things you cannot know.
The moonlit dynasties are a thing of the past. Yet even now, with the sun shining high in the sky, there are those who would call forth a dead moon's ghost.
Could that be why Vedrfolnir held back? Or was it because of some court secret he's not at liberty to share?
...I have to get a clear answer from him. No matter what happens, I will protect Tholindis.
(Rerir seems to be very concerned by Vedrfolnir's reaction...)
(Vedrfolnir and Dainsleif, "The Visionary" and "Twilight Sword." So that's what they were really like...)
(I've investigated this whole area now. There doesn't seem to be any other memories here.)
(Should I try somewhere else? Wait a second... What's this black smoke?)
So he's late, after all! Just you wait, Rerir... You're in for it, big time!
Are you waiting for someone, Ma'am? Could I tempt you into buying some flowers?
Hm? Oh, sure. Pick me out a pretty bunch, if you would.
Thank you! But I'm afraid none of them are as pretty as you...
For someone so young, you sure have a way with words, don't you?
I'm only telling the truth. Look me in the eyes... you'll see I'm not lying.
You're...
May we have a word in private?
...Who are you, and what do you want?
It doesn't matter who I am. Too many of our kind have fallen lately, so I decided to take the risk of reaching out.
Not long ago, the Rächer of Solnari led an assault on one of our strongholds. We suffered many casualties, and many who came to our aid lost their lives as well.
Sorry, I don't know why you're telling me this... and I don't want to get involved.
Wait... Hear me out. This time, we finally got a clear look at his face and learned his true identity.
His name is Rerir, and he claims to be one of the king's guards.
...What did you say!?
A cruel irony, isn't it... the man you're set to marry leads a double life as a brutal executioner. But surely, you must have caught a whiff of the blood on his hands?
Why are you telling me all of this now?
Simple. It's because...
(How strange... Rerir was nowhere to be seen in that memory. It clearly belonged to Tholindis.)
(Rerir couldn't possibly know what happened if he wasn't even there.)
(Why would her memories appear in his fragment?)
(...The ceremony won't last much longer... I think it's time to call it a day.)
So that was your doing? Did you just... pull us inside Rerir's fragment to spy directly on his memories?
Any more questions and I'll have to start charging.
I had no idea you could do that, boss! Seriously, that was amazing... We're not worthy, we're not worthy!
I gotta admit, though, I'm itching to see what happens next... Feels like we barely scratched the surface...
I'm just as curious as you are, but the ceremony only allows for limited time inside. That's all we can see for now.
Luckily, we managed to learn quite a lot.
So far, so good... I just hope the others are doing okay too.
Especially the group with {NICKNAME}... Their mission is a risky one. Let's hope it's all going smoothly.
If you're worried about them, go see how they're doing.
If I know Boss, she's gonna need some time to write up all the details and make sure it's all coherent. I'll stay behind to lend a hand, but feel free to head back and meet up with the others.
